precepts.text: Where no hedge is, there the possession is spoiled. If you do not lead your house, you lose control, and the possession is spoiled. If you are not there guiding, instructing, and correcting, the marriage comes to a crashing halt.
precepts.point: Slides read in class, things husbands do that destroy marriages: adultery and fornication, which has caused damage in Israel beyond repair, so if you are battling that, get help right now; failure to lead; bitterness and harshness, holding things over her head after she has repented, humiliating her, unrealistic expectations; neglect, when a trip to the store is the only outing your wife has had in months, take your wife out, because ordering the house and dealing with the kids is difficult; pride and refusing correction, you ask leadership for counsel, then leave and remix it your own way; financial irresponsibility, wasting money, gambling, hiding spending, chasing image over stability; lack of self control, emotional men punching walls and threatening divorce constantly, saying things that cannot be unsaid; loving the world more than his family, idolizing jobs, status, and friends; failure to dwell with his wife according to knowledge; and withholding love and affection, because if she is not getting it from you, where is she going to get it from?
precepts.why:
“Where no hedge is, there the possession is spoiled.” A bishop must be “One that ruleth well his own house”, and a man who will not lead his house has no hedge around it. If you don’t lead your house, you are going to lose control, and your possession, your wife, will be spoiled.

Failure to lead is one of the things husbands do that destroy marriages. Not stepping up, not taking control of your home, being a passive individual while your wife walks all over you. Eventually some other man is going to come along who catches her eye, and she is going to desire and look to him. Coach Dingolane destroyed a house that way, all because a man would not step up and lead his home.

The flock of God’s pasture are men, and leaders are men. If you are not there guiding, not there instructing, not there correcting, the marriage will come to a crashing halt with her standing over you.

That is why Paul asks, “For if a man know not how to rule his own house, how shall he take care of the church of God?” How can you lead other men and tell them this is the way, if your own house is out of order, if your wife doesn’t listen to you and your kids don’t listen to you? You cannot be over men if you are not able to rule your own house. And the qualities of a bishop are for every man: a bishop is an example of what we are all supposed to be.

precepts.text: Likewise, ye husbands, dwell with them according to knowledge, giving honour unto the wife, as unto the weaker vessel. A wise husband studies his wife: her fears, emotions, struggles, and strengths. When you understand your wife, you know her limits, and you set things up in the home so things can work. Some men never learn their wives and then wonder why the marriage feels distant.
precepts.point: Slides read in class, things husbands do that destroy marriages: adultery and fornication, which has caused damage in Israel beyond repair, so if you are battling that, get help right now; failure to lead; bitterness and harshness, holding things over her head after she has repented, humiliating her, unrealistic expectations; neglect, when a trip to the store is the only outing your wife has had in months, take your wife out, because ordering the house and dealing with the kids is difficult; pride and refusing correction, you ask leadership for counsel, then leave and remix it your own way; financial irresponsibility, wasting money, gambling, hiding spending, chasing image over stability; lack of self control, emotional men punching walls and threatening divorce constantly, saying things that cannot be unsaid; loving the world more than his family, idolizing jobs, status, and friends; failure to dwell with his wife according to knowledge; and withholding love and affection, because if she is not getting it from you, where is she going to get it from?
precepts.why:
“Likewise, ye husbands, dwell with them according to knowledge, giving honour unto the wife, as unto the weaker vessel.” Failure to dwell with his wife according to knowledge is another of the things husbands do that destroy marriages, and ruling your own house well depends on it.

A wise husband studies his wife: her fears, her emotions, her struggles, her strengths. That is dwelling with her according to knowledge. When you understand your wife, you are able to guide your house. You push her toward greatness, but you also know her limits, and because you know them you set things up in the home so that things can work. If your wife is emotionally not there to deal with certain things, then you set it up another way. In order to lead, you have to know what they deal with, what they are able to do and what they are not able to do. That goes for your kids as well. You do it now without realizing it: you understand strengths and weaknesses, and you prioritize based on that.

Some men never learn their wives and then wonder why the marriage feels distant.

The other things that destroy a house show the same failure to know her: bitterness and harshness, holding things over her after she has repented and humiliating her, when you are supposed to love your wife as your own self; neglect, when a trip to Walmart is an exciting event for her because you haven’t taken her out, while ordering the house and dealing with the kids all the time is difficult; and withholding love and affection, because if she is not getting it from you, where is she going to get it from? A bishop rules his own house well by dwelling with his wife according to knowledge and giving her honour.

precepts.text: Not a novice: a novice means a beginner, a newbie, a neophyte. Lest being lifted up with pride he fall into the condemnation of the devil: I know all the precepts. His head gets big cuz he thinks he knows it all. That's young men, and this type of spirit will destroy himself. So that's who Rehoboam looked to. Some of y'all in here make that same mistake.
precepts.point: King Rehoboam sent Adoram, who was over the tribute, and all Israel stoned him with stones, that he died., you came in to collect money? We ain't giving you nothing. And Rehoboam made speed to get him up to his chariot to flee to Jerusalem; he said, they going to kill me next. So Israel rebelled against the house of David unto this day.

note.label: Raising Up the Tabernacle of David That Fell

precepts.why:
Rehoboam “forsook the counsel of the old men, which they had given him, and consulted with the young men that were grown up with him”. Those are his peers. Notice the difference: to the old men he asked, “How do ye advise that I may answer this people?” To the young men, “What counsel give ye that we may answer this people”? We, all together: y’all are my peers, we are running this thing.

Paul warns about that kind of counsel: “Not a novice, lest being lifted up with pride he fall into the condemnation of the devil.” A novice is a beginner, a newbie, a neophyte. Lifted up with pride: I know all the precepts. His head gets big because he thinks he knows it all. That is young men, and that type of spirit will destroy itself.

So that is who Rehoboam looked to, and the young men told him to say, “My little finger shall be thicker than my father’s loins.” Some of you in here make that same mistake.

precepts.text: This is how they gauged choosing the seven: the deacons must be grave, not doubletongued, not given to much wine, not greedy of filthy lucre, and first be proved. And even so must their wives be grave, not slanderers, sober, faithful in all things. You didn't just look at the man; you looked at his wife too. If your wife is low down and no good, that is a reflection on you, brother.
precepts.point: The high priest told him that there was such money laid up for the relief of widows and fatherless children, and that some of it belonged to Hircanus son of Tobias, a man of great dignity, and not as that wicked Simon had misinformed: in all four hundred talents of silver and two hundred of gold. And that it was altogether impossible that such wrong should be done unto them that had committed it to the holiness of the place.
precepts.why:
The apostles said, look out “seven men of honest report, full of the Holy Ghost and wisdom”, to take care of the widows. You may ask, what did they base choosing these men on? Timothy shows how they gauged it.

“Likewise must the deacons be grave, not doubletongued, not given to much wine, not greedy of filthy lucre; Holding the mystery of the faith in a pure conscience. And let these also first be proved; then let them use the office of a deacon, being found blameless.”

Then: “Even so must their wives be grave, not slanderers, sober, faithful in all things. Let the deacons be the husbands of one wife, ruling their children and their own houses well.” You didn’t just look at the man; you looked at his wife too. Sometimes you find a brother who appears decent, but his wife is ratchet, low down, no damn good. That’s a reflection on you, brother. If your wife is low down and no good, you ain’t guiding her right.

So they looked at the man, then they looked at the wife, and said, he has wisdom, he is of honest report, and they chose seven. The ones trusted with what belongs to the widows and the fatherless had to be proved and blameless, the very opposite of a man like Simon, a betrayer of the money.

precepts.text: Moreover he must have a good report of them which are without. Onias had a good report among the Jews and the other nations, and he was not trying to join with the other nations. Without means outside the truth: you must have a good report outside this truth.
precepts.point: Not only the Jews, but many also of other nations, took great indignation, and were much grieved for the unjust murder of the man, because Onias had a good report even among the other nations. The king was heartily sorry, and moved to pity, and wept, because of the sober and modest behaviour of him that was dead; and being kindled with anger, he took away Andronicus his purple, rent off his clothes, led him through the whole city unto that very place where he had committed impiety against Onias, and there slew he the cursed murderer. Thus the Lord rewarded him his punishment, as he had deserved.
precepts.why:
When Onias was murdered, “not only the Jews, but many also of other nations, took great indignation, and were much grieved for the unjust murder of the man”, and even Antiochus “was heartily sorry, and moved to pity, and wept, because of the sober and modest behaviour of him that was dead.” The white man was crying for Onias, because other nations respected Onias III.

That is his character. He had a good report among the Jews and among the other nations, and he was not trying to join with the other nations; he said, I'm not joining with you. But he still had a good report among them. “Moreover he must have a good report of them which are without; lest he fall into reproach and the snare of the devil.”

“Without” means without the truth. You must have a good report outside this truth. If we are at camp one day and somebody tries to do a drive-by on us because of something you did or said, what the hell is going on here? You have to have a good report within and without, like Onias.

precepts.text: If a man know not how to rule his own house: it is your job, not leadership's, to rule it.
precepts.point: Counsel is given twice on the same matter; if it is not fixed, both of you are wrong and you are wasting my time. Leadership gives the scriptures; it cannot make a husband love you or a wife respect you, and those who fix it never come back.
precepts.why:
“Marriage is honourable in all.” Who makes a marriage honourable? Both sides applying the scriptures, the man and the woman loving their neighbour as themselves and dealing right with each other. A marriage does not become honourable just like that. Being an Israelite married to an Israelite sister does not make it honourable, because some are dishonourable brothers and dishonourable sisters: vessels to dishonour who hate each other, fight and argue all the time, speak evil about each other, with no love in the house. Those marriages are not honourable.

“For if a man know not how to rule his own house, how shall he take care of the church of God?” This is what the brothers have to understand. It is not up to leadership to rule you men or to rule your house for you. It is not our job to tell your wife to respect you. It is your job to rule your own damn house.

A lot of you come for counsel, and counsel is given twice on the same matter. If you are counselled twice and it isn’t fixed, you aren’t listening, you are wasting our time, and something is wrong with both of you. Couples come for advice, then a couple of months later: I hate you, I hope you die; and on the Sabbath, shalom, brother, Most High and Christ bless. You are fake and phony. Leaders, stop counselling the dishonourable, hateful brothers and sisters over and over; let them learn online, and deal with the people who really want help.

Leadership’s job is to give you the scriptures so you can fix yourself; it cannot fix you. We cannot force your husband to love you; it is up to you to be a good wife. And brothers, we cannot make your wife respect and love you; you have to figure out how to fix that. The ones who fix it never come back: the brother says yes, I understand, goes home and fixes it, and the sister fixes it. The key is that people have to see their own faults. Some are always looking for somebody to blame, and they will blame leadership, but ruling the house is the man’s charge.

precepts.text: Not a novice, lest being lifted up with pride he fall into the condemnation of the devil. Too much rain on a new seed corrupts it.
precepts.point: Man is formed with God's hands, called his own image, and likened unto the husbandman's seed.
precepts.why:
Ezra says the husbandman's seed perishes “if it come not up, and receive not thy rain in due season; or if there come too much rain, and corrupt it”. The husbandman is the Most High, the seed is the word he sows in us, and the rain is wisdom. Anyone who has planted knows that if too much rain falls on a seed, it does not grow. How can too much rain corrupt a man? Paul shows it: “Not a novice, lest being lifted up with pride he fall into the condemnation of the devil.”

A novice is somebody new in this truth, a beginner. Some brothers come in and catch on real quick. Why would a novice get lifted up with pride? Because he got too much rain, too much wisdom, and he cannot handle it. He starts getting high-minded, and then he falls into the condemnation of the devil: Satan destroys the seed that is in him. That is what it means when the scripture says too much rain can corrupt the seed. Knowledge puffeth up, but charity edifieth.

That is why the heavy teaching is eased off at times. You may love it when the class goes deep, but too much of that wisdom too fast can corrupt you. The deacons have been learning in this truth for over twenty years. When you see them go into certain things, it comes from years of being watered; nobody woke up one day able to break down the scriptures.

So the Most High gives the rain in its season, moderately, as Joel says, “the former rain moderately”, raising the waters little by little, from the ankles to the knees, so that we can handle it. The seed that receives its rain in due season takes root and bears fruit; the novice who is lifted up with pride perishes like the corrupted seed.

precepts.text: If a man desire the office of a bishop, he desireth a good work.
precepts.point: To be full of the Holy Ghost is first and foremost to be keeping the laws. The office is desired by your works, your dedication, and your natural love for your people, not by gunning for a title. Moses was made a leader because he defended his people, and David showed the attributes of a leader wrestling lions and bears and facing Goliath before he was ever called.

note.label: Acts 6: The Grecians Were Greek-Speaking Israelites

precepts.why:
“This is a true saying, If a man desire the office of a bishop, he desireth a good work.”

The office is a work, and it is desired by your works, your dedication and your natural love for your people, not by gunning for a title. Moses was made a leader because he defended his people, and David showed the attributes of a leader wrestling lions and bears and facing Goliath before he was ever called. Just as the daily ministration had a criterion, rank and order has a criterion, and the seven men of honest report were chosen by it.

precepts.why:
“A bishop then must be blameless, the husband of one wife, vigilant, sober, of good behaviour, given to hospitality, apt to teach”.

The husband of one wife shows why other camps that push multiple wives neither have the character nor the desire to build a nation. Their focus is on fulfilling sexual desires, not the work, which requires a man to travel and teach every day. The greats, Marcus Garvey, Martin Luther King, Nat Turner, kept one wife because their focus was the work. Blameless, vigilant, sober, apt to teach: that is what honest report and full of wisdom look like.
